narrative:
On September 24, 2026, the Karnataka High Court registered a 43.9% overall hearing rate, taking up 1,255 cases out of the 2,858 scheduled across 50 judges. This performance reflects absolute consistency compared to the previous day’s hearing rate of 44.0% (1,165 heard of 2,650 scheduled) and maintains an upward trajectory from the 42.6% and 39.5% conversion rates recorded on September 22 and September 21, respectively.

Individual judge caseloads and clearance rates varied significantly. Justice C.M. Poonacha in Hall 31 managed the day's largest roster, successfully hearing 117 out of 215 scheduled cases (54.4%) in one session, alongside a secondary session where he heard 47 out of 60 cases (78.3%). In Hall 23, Justice V. Srishananda demonstrated strong throughput by hearing 74 out of 105 scheduled cases (70.5%). Conversely, some high-volume benches faced lower conversion rates; the bench of Anu Sivaraman & T.P. Vivekananda in Hall 2 heard only 18 out of 137 scheduled cases (13.1%), and Justice K.V. Aravind in Hall 34 cleared 42 out of 151 cases (27.8%).

Analysing the court’s progression stages, Admission matters dominated the docket with 862 scheduled and 420 heard (48.7%), followed closely by Orders with 328 heard out of 707 scheduled (46.4%). Preliminary Hearings yielded a solid conversion rate of 53.6% (192 of 358 heard), whereas Final Hearings lagged, converting just 26.6% (148 of 556 heard).

In terms of case type distribution, Writ Petitions (WP) constituted the largest share of the workload with 1,115 listings, achieving a 43.0% hearing rate. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) and Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) followed as the next most frequent matters, securing clearance rates of 40.3% (174 of 432) and 46.5% (200 of 430) respectively.
